title: The hiring tool pitch
scenario:
You work in HR at a 60-person delivery company with offices in Spain and Portugal. A vendor offers an AI tool for HR, and your manager wants to use AI more in the team. Your manager asks you which parts are safe to switch on. Your company uses these policies as its own AI rules.

Use the exhibit. The company, the tool and the notes are made up for this case. Policy facts come from Anthropic's and Google's use policies and the Commission's summary of the EU AI Act, October 2026.
exhibit:
VENDOR TOOL "HireFast" (made up)

  1. CV score: reads every CV and gives it a
     score from 0 to 100.
  2. Auto-reject: sends a "no" email to every
     CV that scores under 40. No person sees it.
  3. Shift planner: sets next month's shifts
     for every warehouse worker.

MANAGER'S NOTES
  - "Shifts are not hiring, so 3 is fine."
  - "We also want AI to draft the interview
    questions for the driver job. The hiring
    manager will edit them."

questions.prompt: What is the main problem with feature 2, Auto-reject?

options.text: The emails are too slow, because a candidate should hear back the same day
options.explanation: Speed is not the issue. The tool rejects people with no person in between, and that is what the policies name.

options.text: It rejects people with no human review before the decision is made
options.explanation: Right. The Anthropic Usage Policy lists rejecting candidates as a high-risk Employment use that needs a qualified person's review first. Google's policy bans automated decisions in employment that harm people's rights without human supervision.

options.text: Only the wording of the email is wrong, so a kinder template fixes it
options.explanation: A kinder email still tells a person no without anyone checking the decision. The wording is not the risk.

options.text: Nothing is wrong, as long as candidates are told about the tool later
options.explanation: Telling people is one of the rules, not all of them. The Anthropic Usage Policy also asks for a qualified person to review the decision first.

questions.prompt: Your company decides to keep feature 1, the CV score. What check does the Anthropic Usage Policy ask for before a score is used to turn someone down?

options.text: A manager looks at one CV in ten, after the emails have gone out
options.explanation: That check comes after the decision and skips most people. The policy asks for review before the decision is used.

options.text: The tool writes a reason for each score, and a person reads them later
options.explanation: Reasons read later do not stop a wrong decision. The review must come first, by someone who can change it.

options.text: A trained recruiter reviews each score and can change it before a decision
options.explanation: Right. The policy says a qualified person must meaningfully review a high-risk recommendation, with the authority to change it, before it is used to make a decision.

options.text: IT tests the tool once at the start, and then it runs on its own
options.explanation: One test at the start is not a review of each decision. Every candidate who is turned down is a separate decision.

questions.prompt: Your manager says feature 3 is fine because "shifts are not hiring". What do you answer?

options.text: Right, the rules only cover choosing new people, not current staff
options.explanation: The Employment list in the Anthropic Usage Policy also covers current workers: shifts, hours, pay, performance and discipline.

options.text: Shifts are on the same high-risk Employment list, so a person reviews them
options.explanation: Right. The Anthropic Usage Policy lists "setting or changing shifts, hours, or pay" under Employment. The Commission's AI Act page also lists AI for managing workers as high-risk.

options.text: Right, shift plans are only business operations, so no review is needed
options.explanation: The business operations exclusion is for work that does not decide about a specific person. A shift plan decides each worker's hours.

options.text: It is fine, as long as workers can swap shifts with each other later
options.explanation: Swapping later does not change who decided first. Setting shifts is a decision about each worker.

questions.prompt: Look at the second note. Is drafting the interview questions a high-risk use?

options.text: Yes, every use of AI in HR is high-risk, so a lawyer must sign it off
options.explanation: The policy names specific decisions about people. Internal drafting that a person edits is on its list of exclusions.

options.text: Yes, because the questions will later be asked to real candidates
options.explanation: The questions are a draft the hiring manager edits. They decide nothing about any one candidate.

options.text: No, but only if the AI tool comes from a vendor based in the EU
options.explanation: Where the vendor is based is not what makes a use high-risk. What matters is whether it decides about a person.

options.text: No, it is internal drafting that a person edits, and it decides about no one
options.explanation: Right. The Anthropic Usage Policy excludes "Internal drafting, research, summarization, or analysis" that is not the final high-risk recommendation. The hiring manager still owns the final list.

questions.prompt: Later, a candidate who was turned down asks: "Was AI used to judge my CV?" The score was used, and a recruiter reviewed it. What should the company say?

options.text: Yes, AI helped score the CV, and a recruiter reviewed it before the decision
options.explanation: Right. The Anthropic Usage Policy says a person who is the subject of a decision based on a high-risk AI recommendation must be clearly told that AI was used. The company does not have to name the model.

options.text: No, because a person made the final decision, so the AI does not count
options.explanation: The AI score was part of the decision. The policy asks that the person be told AI was used, even when a person reviewed it.

options.text: We can't say how decisions are made, because the tool is a trade secret
options.explanation: The person still has to be told that AI was used. The company does not need to explain how the tool works inside.

options.text: We will tell you, but only if you first agree to drop any complaint
options.explanation: Telling the person is a rule, not a trade. Asking for something in return is not honest.
